definition: Cerebral palsy is a group of lifelong movement disorders caused by brain injury or abnormal brain development occurring before birth, around birth, or in the first few years of life. It does not progressively worsen, but motor difficulties can range from mild problems with fine movement to severe stiffness affecting all limbs; common forms include spastic, athetoid, ataxic, and mixed types.
